answer: A cheap farm can spin up names faster than a forest grows timber, unless each new identity must bind itself to a fresh, unpredictable chain artifact. Ask every applicant to explain a recent state root in their own words and to post a small bond that unlocks only after several epochs of independent, non-cloned behavior. A copied plume of near-identical essays, or answers that ignore the latest nebula of chain noise, is an easy reject. The bond makes mass identity expensive; the moving target makes precomputed templates worthless.
